newsitem.title: USA: Cerion sees Q4 challenges continuing.
newsitem.headline: Cerion sees Q4 challenges continuing.

text.p: Cerion Technologies Inc said it expects results in 1997, especially the first half, to be affected by challenges seen in the fourth quarter.

"While we will continue to control costs and pursue new business opportunities aggressively, we believe similar challenges that affected our fourth quarter results will continue to have an effect on our financial performance for 1997, particularly in the first half," said David Peterson, chief executive of the computer disk substrates maker.
For the year ended December 31, Cerion reported net sales of $36.5 million, compared with $28.2 million in 1995.
Net income for 1996 was $2.5 million, or $0.39 per share, compared with net income of $3.4 million, or $0.64 per share.

"During the fourth quarter, we faced ... increased industry pricing pressures, coupled with a drastic reduction in orders from a major customer due to backwards integration and lower-than-anticipated orders from other customers," Peterson said.

"To begin to address key issues resulting from these challenges, we reduced the number of salaried employees to contain costs and returned to a five-day-week manufacturing schedule. We will take the necessary steps to bring manufacturing costs in line with new pricing standards in the industry," Peterson said.
